L2519@P59: Session thu-p-a : Spectral unmixing
L2520@P59: STRUCTURED SPARSE BAYESIAN HYPERSPECTRAL COMPRESSIVE SENSING USING SPECTRAL UNMIXING
L2521@P59: Lei Zhang, Wei Wei, Yanning Zhang, Fei Li and Hangqi Yan
L2522@P59: School of Computer Science, Northwestern Polytechnical University, Xian, China
L2523@P59: Abstract : To reduce huge consumption of processing hyperspectral images(HSI), a novel Bayesian unmixing compressive
L2524@P59: sensing framework is proposed to compress and reconstruct HSI effectively, called structured sparse Bayesian umixing compressive
L2525@P59: sensing(SSBUCS). SSBUCS unites compressive sensing and hyperspectral linear mixed model in Bayesian framework. An HSI is
L2526@P59: decomposed as a linear combination of endmembers and abundance matrix. The abundance matrix is transformed to a structured
L2527@P59: sparse signal in the wavelet domain. Then, compressive sensing is employed on this sparse signal to produce a more compact result.
L2528@P59: To recover the HSI, a Markov chain Monte Carlo(MCMC) method based on Gibbs sampling is proposed, imposing structured sparse
L2529@P59: prior on abundance matrix. Experimental results verify the superiority of the proposed method over several state-of-art methods.
L2530@P59: Sparse unmixing via WM algorithm for hyperspectral images
L2531@P59: Ion Marques Student Member, IEEE, and Manuel Graña Member, IEEE
L2532@P59: Abstract : Spectral unmixing aims to estimate the fractional abundances of spectral signatures in each pixel. The Linear Mixing Model (LMM) of hyperspectral images assumes that pixel spectra are affine combinations of fundamental spectral signatures called
L2533@P59: endmembers. Endmember induction algorithms (EIA) extract the endmembers from the hyperspectral data. The WM algorithm assumes that a set of Affine Independent vectors can be extracted from the rows and columns of dual Lattice Autoassociative Memories
L2534@P59: (LAAM) built on the image spectra. Indeed, the set of endmembers induced by this algorithm defines a convex polytope covering the
L2535@P59: hyperspectral image data. However, the number of endmembers extracted can be huge. This calls for additional endmember selection
L2536@P59: steps, and to approaching the unmixing problem with linear sparse regression techniques. In this paper, we combine WM algorithm
L2537@P59: with clustering techniques and Conjugate Gradient Pursuit (CGP) for endmember induction. Our experiments are conducted using
L2538@P59: hyperspectral imaging obtained by the Airborne Visible/Infrared Imaging Spectometer of the NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory.
L2539@P59: ENDMEMBER CONSTRAINED SEMI-SUPERVISED HYPERSPECTRAL UNMIXING
L2540@P59: Jakob Sigurdsson, Magnus O. Ulfarsson and Johannes R. Sveinsson, University of Iceland, Dept. Electrical Eng., Reykjavik, Iceland
L2541@P59: Abstract : In this paper an endmember constrained semi-supervised hyperspectral unmixing method is proposed. The
L2542@P59: linear model is used to represent the hyperspectral data. A priori information about the endmembers is incorporated into the
L2543@P59: objective function with soft regularization. This information can be acquired from a spectral library or from the data itself. Quantitative evaluation of the method is done using simulated data and it is shown the soft regularization can yield better results than
L2544@P59: hard regularization. The method is also applied on a real hyperspectral data set and the estimated abundance maps improve when
L2545@P59: a priori information is used to aid the unmixing.
L2546@P59: VALIDATING NONLINEAR MIXING MODELS: BENCHMARK DATASETS FROM VEGETATED AREAS
L2547@P59: L. Tits, KU Leuven - Dept. of biosystems, Geomatics Lab, BE-3001 Leuven, Belgium
L2548@P59: B. Somers, KU Leuven - Division Forest, Nature and Landscape, BE-3001 Leuven, Belgium
L2549@P59: J. Stuckens, Merkator NV, BE-1731 Zellik, Belgium
L2550@P59: P. Coppin, KU Leuven - Dept. of biosystems, Geomatics Lab, BE-3001 Leuven, Belgium
L2551@P59: Abstract : Our understanding of nonlinear mixing events in vegetated areas is currently hampered by a pertinent lack
L2552@P59: of well-validated datasets. Most quantification and modeling efforts are based on theoretical assumptions or indirect empirical
L2553@P59: observations. In this study, a physically based ray tracer was used to create simulated hyperspectral datasets of vegetative systems.
L2554@P59: This model incorporates multiple scattering effects, and nonlinear mixing behavior can be observed in the rendered data. The
L2555@P59: main benefit of the ray-tracer is that we were able to demonstrate with in situ measurements that both the nature and the intensity
L2556@P59: of the nonlinear mixing events are realistically modeled. Different ray-tracer datasets will be made available to the wider scientific
L2557@P59: community as a benchmark dataset to test and validate new and existing unmixing methodologies. In this contribution, we would
L2558@P59: like to present the structure of these datasets, and show how they can be used to evaluate nonlinear mixing models. In addition,
L2559@P59: and maybe even more important, we would like to draw the attention to the limitations of the data, as well point out the assumptions made in the construction of the data.
